subject: Reserved pool tokens/sec addendum and fallback playbook — renewal
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@orionmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity expansion: tokens/sec addendum proposal

Claire —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Per our discussion, OrionMed's renewal will combine a 12‑month term extension with an expansion of the dedicated reserved pool (add 12 A100s equivalent) to support the new diagnostic inference workloads. To keep the app SLAs predictable for your product team, we sketched a tokens/sec guarantee for the reserved pool and an operational fallback playbook if utilization spikes.

I attached a draft addendum (OrionMed_TPS_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and an OPS playbook (tokensps-fallback-playbook.docx) with the following highlights:
- Baseline commitment: 250,000 tokens/sec aggregate for reserved pool during peak windows (08:00–20:00 PT)
- Burst allowance: +20% burst for up to 15 minutes, auto-throttled by queue when needed
- Fallback policy: automated model downgrade to quantized variant + cross-region spill to maintain 99.5% request success for the tiered endpoints
- Credits: pro‑rated service credits for sustained degradation beyond SLO thresholds (detailed table in attached draft)

Ask: can your team confirm whether baseline TPS and the time-window make sense operationally? If Legal wants tighter wording, loop them in and we’ll move to a formal annex.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal review (we'll finalize SLO language and fallback steps) — 48h
2) Legal review on Orion side (we can propose redlines) — target 1 week
3) Execution via DocuSign and capacity provisioning post-execution (2–3 weeks)

-Marketing note: we will not publish performance numbers externally without mutual signoff.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@orionmed.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: OrionMed Legal <legal@orionmed.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity expansion: tokens/sec addendum proposal

Thanks Alex — this looks like a solid starting point. A couple quick clarifying questions before I escalate to Legal:

1) The 250k tokens/sec baseline — is that tied to a specific pool size (number of GPUs) or is it an abstracted throughput guarantee regardless of machine mix?
2) During bursts and cross-region spill, what is the expected P95 latency impact for our edge endpoints? Our clinical workflows have a 500ms soft limit.
3) Can you add an explicit data‑segregation sentence in the playbook confirming that inference logs written during cross-region spill remain encrypted and access limited to OrionMed admins?

Also tagging Legal so they can look at the draft SLA language and propose any redlines.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@orionmed.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity expansion: tokens/sec addendum proposal — SLO language + ops playbook

Claire —

Appreciate the quick review. Below are concrete answers and proposed wording we can drop into the addendum. I've also attached a marked‑up playbook with runbooks and owner assignments.

1) Baseline tie to pool size: 250k tokens/sec is expressed as an aggregate reserved‑pool commitment (pool level), independent of exact machine mix. Wording suggestion: "Redwood will maintain an aggregate minimum reserved pool throughput of 250,000 tokens per second during the Contracted Peak Window (08:00–20:00 PT), measured as system‑level successful token emissions across the reserved pool."

2) Latency expectation during fallbacks: P95 impact guidance — model downgrade to the quantized variant increases P95 by ~120–150ms on average; cross‑region spill adds variable network tail (~40–80ms) depending on route. Combined expected incremental P95: 160–230ms. Wording suggestion: "When fallback policies are executed (quantized model downgrade and cross‑region spill), Redwood anticipates an incremental P95 latency impact of 160–230ms. Redwood will monitor end‑to‑end latency and alert OrionMed when projected P95 exceeds 500ms."

3) Data segregation and encryption: Agree — proposed clause: "All inference request/response logs generated during cross‑region spill or fallback execution shall be encrypted in transit and at rest using customer‑managed KMS keys where configured. Access to those logs will be restricted to OrionMed administrative principals and Redwood personnel on a least‑privilege basis; any access will be logged and auditable."

SLO table (proposed excerpts):
- SLO target: 99.5% successful requests across reserved endpoints during Contracted Peak Window
- Measurement window: 30‑day rolling
- Credit thresholds: 0.5%–1.5% below target => 5%–15% credit band, >1.5% => escalation and executive review

Operational playbook highlights (owners assigned):
- On sustained queue depth >60% for 10 consecutive minutes: autoscale to burst lane (owner: Redwood infra ops)
- If autoscale is saturated: trigger model downgrade (owner: Redwood runtime) and notify OrionMed SREs via PagerDuty
- For cross‑region spill: enable encrypted replication and route small fraction (5–10%) for 30m to validate; increase only after mutual confirmation (owner: Redwood account ops + OrionMed SRE)

I've kept the language intentionally prescriptive so Legal has concrete text to edit. If this looks ok to you, Alex, I can put these paragraphs directly into the PDF and produce DocuSign-ready annex.

Attachments: tokensps-fallback-playbook.docx (runbooks + PagerDuty play name), OrionMed_TPS_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (marked up)

-Neha

Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity expansion: tokens/sec addendum and fallback playbook — next steps

Claire —

This looks great — thanks for the quick turn. From Redwood's side we sign off on the proposed SLO wording Neha drafted. Next steps on our timeline:

1) Neha to drop the marked wording into the PDF and return a DocuSign annex by EOD tomorrow (13 Oct).
2) We’ll provision the additional reserved capacity (12 A100s equivalent) into a staging pool once the annex is executed; billing start date will be the effective date on DocuSign.
3) Karthik will coordinate a joint run (SRE exercise) to validate the fallback within 2 business days of provisioning.

Claire — if OrionMed Legal can provide redlines by EOD Friday (16 Oct), we can keep to the target provisioning/activation dates listed above. If you want, I can set up a 30‑minute touch on Thursday to walk legal through the ops playbook.

DocuSign link will be shared once Neha uploads the annex: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ORIONMED-EXP-2026

Thanks —
Marissa
